title: The relay Setup says recommend can leave a role unmatched
lead: The relay Setup text says `relay-roles recommend` resolves each role to a matching row and reports a role with no matching row as unmatched, as the example matrix does for the architect below size L, instead of claiming it resolves every role.
findings_note: s341 relay 2026-10-17 later note: the Setup text says recommend resolves every role, but the example's architect row matches size L only, so a smaller slice leaves the architect unmatched
boundary: **Not in this slice:** changing `recommend` or any matrix row (r7 stays size L only, by owner decision on 2026-10-17); the generic relay text a project without a matrix gets; bumping the relay contract marker, since this corrects what the text says `recommend` returns and adds no rule an outer session follows.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
s320 (landed 2026-10-16) wrote the Setup sentence in `ROLES_PROPOSE` (`src/slicer/ai.py:382-385`): `recommend` "matches the slice against the matrix and resolves every role, the orchestrator included, to one row". s341 (landed 2026-10-17) gave the example matrix orchestrator rows, but on 2026-10-17 the owner chose to keep the architect row (r7) size L only, so on an S or M slice `recommend` prints `architect  (no matching row)` and its JSON lists `"unmatched": ["architect"]`. The s341 relay hit exactly this: the sentence led its first spec to expect `unmatched == []` on an S item. A matrix a project edits can leave any role unmatched, so the sentence is wrong for every project, not only the example.

Scores: importance 2 because the text is the relay contract an outer session reads at Setup, and it already misled one spec; urgency 1 because `recommend` itself prints the gap and the owner settles the lineup at Setup anyway; effort 1 and size S because it is one sentence, its test and the matching docs. Tree slicer, pass v1.13 beside the other relay follow-ups. Discovered from s341.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/ai.py`, `ROLES_PROPOSE` (around line 382): replace "resolves every role, the orchestrator included, to one row" with text that says it resolves each role, the orchestrator included, to the first matching row, and reports a role no row matches as unmatched (`(no matching row)`, and `unmatched` in the JSON), which the owner fills by naming a row or by dropping that role, as with an architect on a slice below size L in the example matrix.
- `tests/test_relay_roles.py`, `test_AiRelay_Setup_ExplainsCollectiveAcceptanceOverridesAndRouting` (around line 1931): the pinned phrase follows the new text.
- `docs/agents.md` and `docs/commands.md`: any sentence that says `recommend` resolves every role (search with `rg -n "every role" docs`).
- `CHANGELOG.md` under Changed.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body: - `test_AiRelay_Setup_SaysAnUnmatchedRoleIsReported`: with a matrix, the `## Setup` section of `ai relay` names `(no matching row)` and `unmatched`, and no longer contains "resolves every role".

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the failing test and watch it go red.
2. Reword the `ROLES_PROPOSE` sentence; update the pinned phrase in the existing Setup test and the docs.
3. Mutation-check: restoring the old sentence turns the new test red.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `python3.12 tests/affected.py --run`, then the full discover. `slicer check` and `git diff --check` pass.
- `slicer ai relay` in this repo shows the new Setup sentence.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch; the owner lands it.
